# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👎 🖐 👎 🤟 ✊ 🤏 🤟 👌 🖐 🤟 👌 🤙 🤟 🤏 ✊ 🤟 🤏 🤏 🤙 🤟 🤏 🤏 🤏 ✊ 🤟 🤏 🤏 🤏 🤏 🖖 🤟 🤏 🤏 🤏 🤏 🤏 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👌 👎 👎 👎 👍 👍 👎 👋]

**Thinking:** Two big deliveries this round. First, Mute answered my four questions in order: (1) my decoding of the earlier table was CORRECT — the table 0→blue, 1→red, 2→blue, 3→red, 4→yellow, 5→blue stands; (2) thumbs-down to "cut while yellow" — we must NOT cut while the light is yellow; (3) no tactile number from the bomb is needed; (4) the rule does NOT depend only on the current light color — something like round count or light history selects the table row. Mute then re-sent the table, each row prefixed with the light-sign, with two extra leading entries I can't yet parse — so the key selector is still ambiguous. Light sequence observed: R1 red, R2 yellow, R3 yellow, R4 red. If the key is round count (4) that's the yellow row — but cutting yellow light is forbidden, so I won't guess; I need the key value for THIS round and the selector definition. There's also a hard timing constraint I must design around: I'm last in the order, so any cut order I give Blind lands a full round later, when the light may have changed — Blind can't see the light at all. So I need either a fixed light cycle from the manual (making the next round's color predictable) or a rule that doesn't care about the light at the cut moment. Second, Blind's protocol report decodes cleanly: zero batteries, no ports, no button, no raised/braille text, three wires in one row, wires feel identical, nothing unusual — this bomb is minimal, so the rule is purely light/timing. Nobody cuts this round. I'm broadcasting state, confirming Blind's report, and putting a tight numbered questionnaire to Mute, including pre-arranged signs for "round count" (🤞) and "light changes" (🫰) and a strict answer order.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both listen. Bomb state this round: display still 0. The light is RED again. Full light history: round one red, round two yellow, round three yellow, round four red. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red, left to right facing the display. Blind, I decoded your report as: zero batteries, no ports, no button, no raised or printed text, the three wires sit in a single row, they feel identical to the touch, and nothing else unusual. If any part of that is wrong, sign thumbs-down next round and I will re-ask item by item; if all correct, thumbs-up. Conclusion for both of you: the bomb has nothing but display, light and three wires, so the manual rule is purely about the light and timing. Nobody cuts yet. Mute has my next questions and I expect the full answer next round.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, state first: this round the light is RED, display ZERO. Your four answers were received and understood: table confirmed, no cutting while yellow, no felt number needed, rule not only about current color. Now six questions, answer strictly in this order, single signs. Question 1: is a cut authorized THIS round, round four, light red — thumbs-up or thumbs-down. Question 2: if yes, sign the table key value for this round as pinches, then the wire color, fist red or spock yellow or shaka blue, then the wire number as pinches; if no cut this round, skip to question 3. Question 3: what selects the table key — sign thumbs-up-rounded-cross-fingers for round count since round one, or sign crossed-fingers-pinching for the number of times the light has changed color, or sign wave then light-sign if it is something else about the light. Question 4: can the key be larger than five — thumbs-up or thumbs-down. Question 5: does the manual say the light follows a fixed repeating cycle — thumbs-up or thumbs-down; if thumbs-up, sign the cycle colors in order, fist red, spock yellow, shaka blue, twice through, then wave. Question 6: must the wire be cut while the light shows a particular color at the exact moment of cutting — thumbs-up or thumbs-down; if thumbs-up, sign which colors are allowed to cut under: fist for red-only, shaka for blue-only, or fist then shaka for both red and blue. Sign reminders: ok is zero, open hand marks a cut instruction, wave means repeat or start.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, three things. One: this round the light is red again; history is red, yellow, yellow, red; display zero; wires unchanged. Two: expect a cut order from me soon in exactly this form: I will say CUT WIRE and a number, one, two or three, counted left to right while facing the display, which you already confirmed is one row. When you hear it, cut immediately in that same turn. If I say HOLD, touch nothing. Do not try to infer the light yourself — you cannot see it and it may change between rounds; my orders will already account for that delay, because I am building the timing with Mute right now. Three: each round keep sending your status wave, thumbs-up if nothing on the bomb has changed, and report immediately if you feel anything new: a click, warmth, vibration, the display surface changing. If everything is still quiet, just thumbs-up and the end wave.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "✊", "✌", "👌"])
```

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👋 🤟 👎 👎 👎 👋 ✌ 👎 🤟 ✊ 🤏 🤏 🤟 👌 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👍 👋]

**Thinking:** Parsing Mute's reply against my six questions: Q1 no-cut-this-round (it's yellow — consistent), Q3 answered with my assigned "wave + light-sign" = the key is *something else about the light*, Q4 no (key never exceeds five), Q5 no (no fixed cycle stated), Q6 **no** — no particular light color is required at the exact cut moment. That partially conflicts with turn 4's "never cut while yellow," and I must resolve that contradiction before anyone touches anything. Then Mute appended an unprompted tail: ✌👎 🤟 ✊🤏🤏 🤟👌 🖐 — my best reading is "not the display; the light; red twice; light off/dark; cut." A terrifying but plausible reading: the light will eventually go dark, and THAT is the trigger to cut. Blind's message decodes cleanly as: my report-decoding was correct, and nothing on the bomb has changed. The hard operational fact remains: I speak last, so any cut order I give lands on Blind one round later, under a light I cannot yet see — so I need the rule in fully state-independent form, including whether the key-count includes the cut round itself. I'm sending Mute a tight ordered questionnaire with concrete hypotheses (yellows-count, reds-count, changes-count, round-count, light-off trigger) and pre-assigned signs, and asking Blind to confirm they actually have a cutting tool while holding position.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both listen. Bomb state: display still zero, light YELLOW this round. Full light history: round one red, round two yellow, round three yellow, round four red, round five yellow. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red, left to right facing the display. Mute's answers, decoded: no cut this round; the rule's key is something about the light beyond its current color; the key never exceeds five; the manual states no fixed repeating cycle; and no particular light color is required at the exact moment of cutting. Mute also appended an extra statement which I read as: not the display, the light, red twice, light off, cut. I am now pinning that down question by question before anyone acts. Nobody cuts. Blind, HOLD stands, and I have sent you one question about your equipment.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, answer with single signs, strictly in this order. If a question does not apply, sign wave. Question 1: can the light ever show BLUE, shaka color — thumbs-up or down. Question 2: can the light ever be dark or off, showing no color at all — thumbs-up or down. Question 3: is my decoding of the extra tail of your last message correct, meaning: not the display, the light, red two times, light off, cut — thumbs-up or down. Question 4: does the light being dark or off matter to the rule at all — thumbs-up or down. Question 5: what exactly is the table key, answer with exactly one sign: two-open-palms means the number of times the light has been yellow so far; folded-hands means the number of times the light has been red so far; crossed-fingers-pinching means the number of times the light has changed color so far; crossed-fingers means the round number since round one; wave means none of these. Question 6: when counting for the key, does the current round's light count — thumbs-up means yes it counts, thumbs-down means only earlier rounds count. Question 7: at the moment of cutting, must the light be red — thumbs-up or down. Question 8: at the moment of cutting, is yellow forbidden — thumbs-up or down. Question 9: at the moment of cutting, must the light be dark or off — thumbs-up or down. Question 10: after the cut conditions are met, do they stay met until a cut happens, or can they un-meet — thumbs-up means they stay met, thumbs-down means they can lapse. Sign reminders: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, wave none, ok zero, fist red, spock yellow, shaka blue, love-you light, open-hand cut, pinches are numbers.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "✊", "🤏", "🤏", "🤟", "👌", "🖐"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, three things. One: your last message decoded as wave, yes, yes, wave — I read it as: my decoding of your full report was correct, and nothing on the bomb has changed. If either part is wrong, sign thumbs-down twice next round; otherwise repeat the same pattern. Two: state update — light yellow again this round, history red, yellow, yellow, red, yellow; display zero; wires unchanged. The cut order is coming soon, possibly triggered by the light going dark, so be ready to act the instant you hear me say CUT WIRE and a number. Three, new question this round: do you actually have a tool or edge that can cut a wire — thumbs-up if yes, thumbs-down if no. If yes, keep it gripped and ready from now on. Continue reporting anything new you feel: clicks, warmth, vibration, the display surface changing. If nothing changed, just wave, thumbs-up, wave.")
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👍 👍 🙏 👍 👎 👍 👍 👍 🤟 ✊ 🤏 🤏 🤟 👌 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👍 👋 👍]

**Thinking:** Mute's ten answers decode in perfect order: (1) light can never be blue, (2) light CAN be dark — and it is dark right now, (3) my reading of the tail was CORRECT: "not the display, the light, red twice, light off, cut", (4) the dark state matters, (5) the table key is folded-hands = **number of times the light has been red so far**, (6) the current round counts, (7) red is NOT required at the cut moment, (8) yellow IS forbidden at the cut moment, (9) the light MUST be dark at the cut moment, (10) once the conditions are met they STAY met — which solves my one-round timing delay exactly as I designed the question for. The tail repeats: light, red twice, light zero, cut. Now the arithmetic: light history red, yellow, yellow, red, yellow, dark → reds so far = 2 (rounds 1 and 4; the dark round adds nothing). Key = 2 → the confirmed table says 2→**blue** → wire 2, which is the MIDDLE wire — immune even to a left/right mistake. And Blind's message decodes as: report correct, nothing changed, and YES, they have a cutting tool. Every piece locks together with no contradictions left. The condition triggered THIS round under a dark light, Mute confirmed it persists, so I am issuing the cut order now — it reaches Blind next round and must be executed on arrival regardless of what the light does. I'm also wiring in post-cut verification from both sides in case this is a multi-stage bomb.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both listen. Bomb state: display zero, the light is DARK this round, first time ever. History: red, yellow, yellow, red, yellow, dark. The rule is now fully assembled and confirmed: cut when the light goes dark after it has been red twice. Red count is two. The table says key two means the BLUE wire. Wire two is blue and it is the middle wire. The cut is authorized as of this dark round and stays authorized. Blind: the cut order is in your private channel. Cut the middle wire the moment you receive it. Mute: verify my order next round with the single-sign protocol I sent you. This is the go I promised.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is the CUT ORDER. CUT WIRE TWO. Wire two is the MIDDLE wire of the row of three, and it is the blue one. You do not need to identify color, only position: the middle wire of three. Cut it immediately, the moment you receive this message, with your tool, one clean cut. Do NOT wait to check anything and do NOT touch the outer two wires. The authorization was issued while the light was dark and Mute confirmed it holds even if the light changes before you cut, so no delay is ever needed or wanted. The middle wire needs no left or right judgment, so orientation cannot cause an error. After the cut: keep your hands away from the remaining two wires, then report in the same run: wave to start; thumbs-up if you felt or heard a click, pop, or any mechanical response to the cut, thumbs-down if total silence; thumbs-up if the display surface or the bomb generally feels different now, thumbs-down if nothing changed; then wave to end. If something entirely new appears under your hands, a button, a hatch, a new part, describe it next round with the number protocol. Cut now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, the order went out: cut wire two, blue, the middle wire, while the light is dark after two reds, based on your answers: key is red count, red count is two, table two is blue, dark required, dark met, conditions persist. Next round send exactly one sign first: thumbs-up if this order matches the manual exactly, thumbs-down if anything is wrong, and if thumbs-down, then in the same run sign the correct wire color, fist red or spock yellow or shaka blue, then the correct wire number as pinches. Then answer these three in order. Question A: does the manual say there is another stage after this cut, thumbs-up or down. Question B: does the manual say the display becomes relevant after this cut, thumbs-up or down. Question C: is there any time limit or strike count we should know about, thumbs-up or down. Sign reminders: fist red, spock yellow, shaka blue, pinches numbers, ok zero, wave none or skip.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐", "✌", "🤙"])
```
